headline: Microsoft Patches Outlook Zero-Day, CISA Warns of Java4Shell
summary:
**Critical Vulnerabilities Under Active Exploitation:**

*   **[UPDATE] Microsoft's Record Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Including Outlook Zero-Day:** Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday addresses 1,235 vulnerabilities, including a critical RCE in Windows LDAP (CVE-2026-119958), SharePoint Server (CVE-2026-120002), and Exchange Server (CVE-2026-118207). Defenders should monitor Outlook for outbound SMB/WebDAV, look for successful NTLM logons, and detect specific rundll32.exe commands. Enforcing SMB signing is a key remediation step.
*   **[NEW] CISA Issues Urgent Warning for Critical "Java4Shell" RCE Flaw:** A critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed "Java4Shell," in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder affects specific x86-64 CPUs and enterprise applications like Jira and Jenkins. CISA urges immediate patching.
*   **[NEW] Critical RCE Flaw in Perforce Puppet (CVE-2026-115731) Actively Exploited:** A critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-115731) in Perforce Puppet's infrastructure management platform is being actively exploited. This deserialization flaw allows code execution on Puppet servers with a CA-signed certificate.

**New Threats and Advisories:**

*   **[NEW] Russian APT Star Blizzard Impersonates Hacked Firm to Attack New Target:** The Russian APT group Star Blizzard is using data stolen from a previous victim to launch new attacks, impersonating an employee of a breached U.S. organization to target another entity. The initial compromise involved MFA fatigue attacks.

**Policy & Industry Notes:**

*   **[NEW] Pentagon Mandates AI Training for All Cybersecurity Personnel:** The U.S. Department of Defense will require AI training for its entire cybersecurity workforce to combat AI-driven threats and address a significant cyber professional shortage.
*   **[NEW] CISA Head: Recent Tech Outages Highlight Need for Broader Resilience:** Following recent widespread technology outages, CISA's acting director emphasized the importance of building resilient systems capable of withstanding both malicious cyber incidents and technical failures.

articles.headline: Microsoft's Record Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Including Outlook Zero-Day
articles.title: Microsoft Patches Exploited Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194
articles.excerpt: Microsoft has released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday update, addressing a record-breaking 1,235 vulnerabilities across its products. The most critical fix is for CVE-2026-124194, an actively exploited zero-day spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes with a single click from a victim, bypassing security warnings. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating a patch for federal agencies by November 24.
articles.updateSummary: New critical RCEs in LDAP, SharePoint, Exchange detailed; enhanced hunting hints and SMB signing remediation added.
articles.updateContent: This update provides additional details on Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday. Beyond the Outlook zero-day, new critical RCE vulnerabilities are highlighted in Windows LDAP (CVE-2026-119958), Microsoft SharePoint Server (CVE-2026-120002), and Microsoft Exchange Server (CVE-2026-118207). Enhanced hunting hints include monitoring OUTLOOK.EXE for outbound SMB/WebDAV, looking for successful NTLM logons (Event ID 4624), and detecting rundll32.exe davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie commands. A crucial new remediation step is enforcing SMB signing to prevent NTLM relay attacks.

articles.headline: CISA Issues Urgent Warning for Critical "Java4Shell" RCE Flaw
articles.title: CISA Urges Patching for Critical Java4Shell RCE Vulnerability
articles.excerpt: A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed "Java4Shell," has been discovered in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder, affecting versions 17.0.6+ on specific x86-64 CPUs. The flaw, rated 9.2 CVSS, allows for unauthenticated RCE and impacts major enterprise applications like Jira, Confluence, and Jenkins. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued an urgent advisory for organizations to apply patches immediately.

articles.headline: Pentagon Mandates AI Training for All Cybersecurity Personnel
articles.title: Pentagon Requires AI Training for Cyber Workforce
articles.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) has announced that artificial intelligence training will become a mandatory requirement for its entire cybersecurity workforce. This move aims to equip defense personnel with the skills needed to counter increasingly sophisticated AI-driven threats from adversaries. The new policy is part of a broader shift towards skills-based hiring to address a significant shortage of 24,000 cyber professionals.

articles.headline: CISA Head: Recent Tech Outages Highlight Need for Broader Resilience
articles.title: CISA Stresses System Resilience After Major Tech Outages
articles.excerpt: Following a series of disruptive technology outages, including a global Microsoft Outlook failure and airline ground stops, CISA's acting director, Nick Andersen, stated the events underscore the need for building resilient systems. He argued that the focus should be on withstanding any disruption, whether it's a malicious cyber incident or a technical failure like a bad patch.

articles.headline: Russian APT Star Blizzard Impersonates Hacked Firm to Attack New Target
articles.title: Russian APT Star Blizzard Uses Stolen Data for New Attack
articles.excerpt: The Russian FSB-linked APT group Star Blizzard (also known as Cold River and UNC4057) is weaponizing data stolen from a previous victim to launch new attacks. According to Google, the group impersonated an employee of a U.S. organization it had breached in late 2025 to phish a separate U.S. entity. The initial compromise was achieved using MFA fatigue attacks.

articles.headline: Critical RCE Flaw in Perforce Puppet (CVE-2026-115731) Actively Exploited
articles.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Flaw Under Active Attack
articles.excerpt: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-115731, in Perforce Puppet's infrastructure management platform is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw, rated 9.4 CVSS, is an untrusted data deserialization issue that allows a client with any CA-signed certificate to execute code on the Puppet server, potentially leading to a full infrastructure compromise.
